title: Improved method for enumerating sulfate-reducing bacteria using optical density
author: Bernardez, de Andrade Lima

steps.title: Acridine orange staining of SRB
steps.instruction: Stain harvested sulfate‑reducing bacteria (SRB) with acridine orange for fluorescence microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Grow SRB in modified Postgate medium and harvest cells in the late exponential phase.
Transfer 1.5 mL of the culture into a clean test tube.
Centrifuge at 10,000 RPM (≈14,310 × g) for 10 min.
Wash the cell pellet twice with PBS buffer.
Resuspend the pellet in 1.0 mL of acridine orange stock solution (prepare stock by dissolving 0.1 g acridine orange in 100 mL sterilized distilled water).
Cover the tube with aluminum foil and incubate in the dark for 30 min.
Place 10 µL of the stained suspension on a clean microscope glass slide.
Immediately observe fluorescence using an Olympus BX51 microscope.

steps.title: Acidify culture and observe reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate SRB culture, then acidify to dissolve iron precipitates and monitor the color change.

substeps.instruction: Transfer aliquots of the culture into an Erlenmeyer flask containing 250 mL of Postgate medium.
Incubate the flask at 38 °C under anaerobic conditions for 120 h to allow optimal growth; a black precipitate (FeS, FeS₂, FeOOH) will form.
Add hydrochloric acid (HCl) dropwise until the mixture reaches pH 2.
Observe the rapid reaction: the dark brown iron sulfide/oxide precipitate dissolves, yielding a clear solution of Fe²⁺.

description: After aliquots of the culture mix were transferred to the Erlenmeyer flask containing 250 mL of Postgate medium and incubated at 38 °C in anaerobic environment for 120 h for optimal growth, a distinct black precipitate became visible after some time. This precipitate could not be readily removed by filtration or centrifugation. The addition of hydrochloride acid (HCl) to the mixture until pH 2 resulted in a rapid reaction, leading to a color change from a dark brown color of FeS, FeS2 and FeOOH to a clear solution of Fe2+. Fig. 1 shows the relationship between the cell concentration expressed as dry biomass and absorbance, reading at 600 nm of SRB cells growing in Postgate standard medium with the addition of HCl to a pH value below 2. In the presence of the acid the experimental data fitted the predicted curve well with a correlation coefficient equal to 0.98. The results with no addition of acid, not shown here, fitted poorly which confirms that the acidification of the medium reduces the iron precipitation and the interference thereof considerably. Fig. 2a and b shows microscopic images of the SRB cells. Fig. 2a shows the SRB cells before acidification and Fig. 2b shows the SRB cells after acidification. After acidification the quality of the image is enhanced while the integrity of the cells seems to be preserved. The bioprocess kinetics were determined in a batch reactor with an initial sulfate concentration of 1790 mg/L. Fig. 3a shows the profiles of residual sulfate (filled triangle symbols) and produced sulfide (cross symbols) concentrations as a function of time. In 360 h (15 days) the sulfate content decreased from 1790 to 22.2 mg/L (a conversion of about 98.8%) and the sulfide concentration increased to 592.6 mg/L. Fig. 3b shows the redox potential measurement (filled diamond symbols), which was used to indicate the bacterial activity due to the reducer character of the SRB.
